- Responsible: Acme provides dataset + acceptance criteria; Redwood runs benchmarks, sets up test harness, and iterates on batching/quantization.
- Dependencies: staging access (VPC/VPN), procurement timeline, sample prompt set and expected pass/fail labels

Attachments: ACME_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf, tech_eval_plan_v1.xlsx (contains benchmarks, datasets, and evaluation harness steps)

Subject: Tech evaluation plan (detailed) — benchmarks, targets, model shortlist

Hi Samantha —

Following up with the technical evaluation plan details you requested. I put the spreadsheet together (attached) but also summarized the key test cases and acceptance criteria below so we have a single place to reference in the MAP.

1) Test harness & datasets\- Test set: 2,000 anonymized support transcripts + 200 targeted eval prompts (edge cases + safety checks)\- Ground truth: binary pass/fail per prompt; rubric in sheet\- Environment: Redwood staging (us-west-2) using a dedicated test project with isolated traffic

2) Quality benchmarks (pass/fail)\- Acceptance: >=95% pass rate across the 200 targeted eval prompts\- Hallucination threshold: <2% high-confidence hallucinations on factual checks

3) Latency + throughput\- Latency targets (512-token budget): p95 < 250ms, p50 < 120ms (measured end-to-end from HTTP client to response completion)
- Throughput: baseline concurrency test at 50 concurrent requests with batching enabled; target sustained tokens/sec that meets your SLA (we'll measure and report)
- Measurement notes: run each model variant with 3 runs, median reported; include KV-cache warm and cold measurements

4) Cost targets\- Hosted per-token cost target: under $3.50 per 1M tokens (based on current Redwood hosted pricing + quantized variants)\- Dedicated cost estimate: we'll include a contrasted cost-per-concurrent-request table in the spreadsheet (depends on reserved GPU profile)

5) Model shortlist & config to test\- Llama-3 34B (FP16 and 4-bit quantized variants)\- Mistral-7B (int8 and FP16)\- Falcon-40B (FP16)\- Redwood-optimized quantized variants (our internal tuned kernels)

6) Responsibilities & timeline\- Acme: provide anonymized dataset, expected pass/fail labels, and staging access (deadline: 2027-05-20)\- Redwood (Camila): run benchmarks, produce result deck with latency/cost/quality, recommend 1–2 model+config options (deliverable: 2027-05-28)\- Marissa: will coordinate procurement and commercial terms; follow up for Dedicated sizing if required

7) Dependencies & risks\- Dependency: VPN/VPC access + sample dataset availability\- Risk: Procurement delays could push Dedicated evaluation beyond target close date — we can run hosted tests in parallel but final pricing for Dedicated will be delayed

I will attach the detailed spreadsheet (tech_eval_plan_v1.xlsx) with test scripts, exact command-line configs, and expected metrics collection. If you want, we can also include a short Jupyter notebook to reproduce the latency tests.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Sam: confirm dataset delivery date and grant staging/project access by 5/20
- Redwood: schedule the benchmark run for the week of 5/24
- Procurement: initial paperwork to be started by 5/25 (per your note)

Happy to jump on the 5/19 kickoff and walk through the spreadsheet.

--
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
